CHIEF COMPLAINT
Left shoulder pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
44-year-old female presenting with left shoulder pain that started one week ago. Patient reports the pain began during a gymnastics class when she fell into an awkward position during a move. She describes the pain as severe and affecting any movement of the left shoulder. Patient attempted self-treatment with Tylenol for 2-3 days without relief. X-ray performed today shows no fracture or broken bone. Physical examination reveals pain with shoulder movement in multiple directions. Clinical impression is joint injury. Patient reports history of prior surgery on left arm but denies current symptoms related to that procedure.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient reports left shoulder pain with any movement. No other systems reviewed.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Prior surgery on left arm.

MEDICATIONS
Tylenol (acetaminophen) - used for 2-3 days, discontinued due to ineffectiveness.

ALLERGIES
Not documented.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient participates in gymnastics class.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Left shoulder: Pain with movement in all directions, including forward and backward motion. No fracture or broken bone noted on x-ray imaging.

RESULTS
X-ray of left shoulder: No fracture or broken bone identified.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Left shoulder joint injury secondary to gymnastics trauma. Plan: (1) Continue pain reliever - ibuprofen 600 mg three times daily for one week; (2) Consider ice or heat pad for symptom relief; (3) Rest left arm and avoid heavy lifting for 3-4 weeks; (4) Use right arm instead for activities; (5) Follow up in 3 weeks to reassess; (6) Consider repeat x-ray at follow-up if pain persists; (7) Patient may contact office if symptoms worsen or for earlier appointment if needed.
